rows.component_basis: liquid RbO0.5 one-cation formula-unit mole fraction; two units per Rb2O parent
rows.parent_standard_state: pure liquid Rb2O at 1 bar over the source's 1673.15–1823.15 K range
rows.source_citation: Sossi, P. A., Klemme, S., O'Neill, H. St.C., Berndt, J. & Moynier, F. (2019), "Evaporation of moderately volatile elements from silicate melts: experiments and theory", Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta 260, 204–231, doi:10.1016/j.gca.2019.06.021
rows.source_locator: Table 4 (PDF p. 57), apparent γi(RbO0.5)=1.3×10−4 at 1673.15 K, 7.4×10−5 at 1773.15 K, and 9.0×10−5 at 1823.15 K; reaction RbO0.5(l)=Rb(g)+1/4 O2; αe=1; FCMAS, 1 bar CO–CO2.
rows.selection_note: Use the printed center-temperature 1773.15 K value 7.4e-5 as the point because the three Table 4 values are nonmonotonic; no log-linear temperature fit is justified.
limitations: apparent activity coefficient calculated with αe=1; not a directly measured melt activity
provisional range law over the three reported temperatures; the band is their min–max and is not a fitted uncertainty interval
Table 4 reports fit precision for the 1673.15 and 1773.15 K values but no uncertainty for the 1823.15 K value

Sossi §4.6 says Table 4 uncertainties are fit precision only and exclude αe, which is close to unity within a factor of 2–3; some inverted Table 4 αe values exceed 1 (Zn 1.7–2.2) and are inversion artifacts
by the open-evaporation Hertz–Knudsen relation, αe=1 gives a lower-bound γ when 0 < αe <= 1 and other terms are fixed
the source composition family is FCMAS
